title: Three-Project Solution Scaffold + IKeychainProvider
keyDecisionsMade: IKeychainProvider.DeleteAsync returns Task (not Task<bool>) as specified in story scope
KeychainProviderFactory.Create(string configDir) takes a non-optional configDir — configDir resolved in Program.cs via EncryptedFileKeychainProvider.GetDefaultConfigDir()
macOS config dir resolved as ~/Library/Application Support/zapi-cli using UserProfile + manual path, not Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData (which gives ~/.config on macOS)
DllImport used instead of LibraryImport for Security.framework P/Invoke — byte[] service/account name params avoid MarshalAs complexity
InMemoryKeychainProvider is thread-safe (uses lock) per story requirement

LinuxKeychainProvider sentinel probe key is '__zapi_cli_probe__'

openQuestionsResolved.resolution: Used SHA256(MachineName + MachineGuid + 'zapi-cli') as AES-256 key. IV is first 12 bytes of .bin file, then ciphertext, then 16-byte GCM tag. MachineGuid: ioreg on macOS, HKLM registry on Windows, /etc/machine-id on Linux.
LinuxKeychainProvider.TryCreate() catches DllNotFoundException and any other error. Performs sentinel probe on init. Returns false to signal fallback to EncryptedFileKeychainProvider.

title: Browser OAuth Infrastructure: LocalCallbackServer + IOAuthBrowserFlow/OAuthBrowserFlow + ErrorCodes
keyDecisionsMade: HttpListener prefix changed from /callback/ to / (root) — HttpListener prefix /callback/ does NOT match requests to /callback?query=string (no trailing slash path). Using / as prefix matches all requests on the ephemeral port, which is safe since we own it exclusively.

Tests use UseProxy=false in HttpClientHandler — a corporate Squid proxy at 127.0.0.1:3128 intercepts localhost HTTP requests and returns 503. Production browser OAuth redirects skip the proxy (browsers bypass proxy for localhost natively). Only tests need UseProxy=false.
OperatingSystem.IsMacOS/IsLinux/IsWindows() used for platform detection in OAuthBrowserFlow (not RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform) to satisfy CA1416 with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true.
TOCTOU retry logic in LocalCallbackServer constructor: catches HttpListenerException on first Start(), retries once with new ephemeral port.
OAuthBrowserFlow.OpenBrowser always prints URL to Console.Error before Process.Start — visible even in piped output, serves as manual-paste fallback.

title: Trace System + trace session Commands

filesCreatedOrModified.action: modified — inject ITraceWriter, capture trace info, write entry after each api call
modified — register trace services + trace command branches

keyDecisionsMade: ApiTraceEntry.Session and ApiTraceEntry.SessionId are NOT 'required' — default to empty string. ApiClient builds entry without these; TraceWriter fills them from the active session via GetActiveSessionAsync.
ApiClient injects ITraceWriter only (not ITraceSession) — TraceWriter handles all session lookups internally. Clean separation: ApiClient provides HTTP data, TraceWriter owns session awareness.

Named Mutex for cross-process safety: on Windows 'Global\zapi-cli-trace-{uuid}', on macOS/Linux 'zapi-cli-trace-{uuid}' (no Global\ prefix — backslash invalid in POSIX semaphore names). RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform used for conditional naming.

Mutex + synchronous I/O via Task.Run wrapping: IncrementEntryCountAsync, UpdateStatusSync (for close/reopen) run sync file I/O inside Task.Run to avoid async/await thread-affinity violation with thread-affine Mutex.
IncrementEntryCountAsync returns -1 on Mutex timeout or session-not-found — TraceWriter checks for seq <= 0 and drops the entry silently with a LogWarning. No exception thrown for timeout.

ITraceSession.StartSessionAsync takes string? requestedExportPath (nullable) — export path resolution (including default config read) happens inside TraceSession.StartSessionAsync. Command stays thin: passes settings.ExportPath directly.

Export path resolution: ends-with-.json → use as exact file path; directory (or null with default configured) → <name>-<uuid[0..8]>.json using first 8 chars of UUID after removing dashes. UUID short-id: sessionId.Replace('-','')[..8].
TraceExporter uses synchronous File.ReadLines (not async) for simplicity — trace files are typically small.

Header key case preservation: Dictionary<string,string> keys are serialized with their original case by System.Text.Json (PolicyNamingPolicy does not apply to dict keys). Unit tests use case-insensitive EnumerateObject() helpers.

TraceWriter.AppendApiEntryAsync is awaited synchronously in ApiClient.CallAsync (not fire-and-forget) to satisfy the 'writes immediately' AC. Uses CancellationToken.None so a ctrl-C after the call still allows the entry to flush.

Sessions.json root is TraceSessionsRoot (inner private class in TraceSession) with List<TraceSessionEntry> Sessions. Serialized with OutputJsonOptions.Shared (SnakeCaseLower) so file keys match CLI output.

openQuestionsResolved.resolution: Name validation: [a-zA-Z0-9_.-], max 64 chars. Regex: @"^[a-zA-Z0-9_.\"-]{1,64}$". No uniqueness check. SESSION_AMBIGUOUS on export/close/reopen/remove by --name when multiple match.
Named Mutex keyed by UUID. WaitOne(2000) — -1 returned on timeout. Task.Run wrapping to avoid async/await thread-affinity issue with Mutex.

Status-based drain: CloseSessionAsync sets 'closing' (step 1), waits waitMs, sets 'closed' (step 3). Both under Mutex. TraceWriter drops entry silently when status='closing' or session is null (closed).
EntryCount NOT reset on reopen. ReopenSessionAsync only changes status to 'active'. IncrementEntryCount reads current EntryCount and increments — seq continues from where it left off.
RemoveSessionAsync removes only the sessions.json entry. Trace file at ExportPath is preserved by design.
Export file name when path is a directory: '<name>-<shortId>.json' where shortId = sessionId.Replace('-','')[..8].

title: Deprecation Warning Infrastructure
keyDecisionsMade: Chose the thin-wrapper command class pattern for deprecated aliases: register a separate command class for each deprecated name that calls DeprecationHelper.Warn() then delegates to the same logic. This avoids Spectre.Console limitations and keeps deprecation paths explicit and grep-able.
DeprecationHelper.Warn() writes to Console.Error unconditionally — no IOutputWriter dependency so it can be called from any command without DI plumbing changes.
Pattern documented in file-level XML doc comment on DeprecationHelper.cs.
